purpose: Finite synthetic acceptance assignments and expected root actions only. No vignette, guideline fidelity, production behavior or clinical performance claim.
truth_semantics: Strong Kleene values plus separately propagated conflict; no closed-world inference for absent facts.

vectors.description: CNF has one FALSE clause even though another atom is TRUE; leaf truth does not satisfy root.
DNF has a complete TRUE branch; FALSE atoms in the other branch do not veto it.
Recursive NOT/OR/AND keeps the intended parenthesis structure.
Missing observation remains UNKNOWN after NOT.
FALSE AND UNKNOWN is definitively FALSE without evaluating an unknown as false.
TRUE OR UNKNOWN is definitively TRUE; the root semantics, not every leaf being known, is decisive.
All unobserved required members stay UNKNOWN; no filtering to an empty AllTrue list.
Positive and negative observations of the same proposition produce UNKNOWN plus conflict.
Root OR is TRUE but unresolved conflict remains explicitly visible.
Each person has an event, which may differ by person: forall p exists e is TRUE.
The same finite model has no single event for all persons: exists e forall p is FALSE.
All observed members satisfy P, but an incomplete domain prevents forall TRUE.
One explicit counterexample refutes forall even when remaining domain members are unknown.
No positive among observed members does not refute exists over an incomplete domain.
A known positive witness proves exists without closing the entire domain.
Classical forall over an explicitly empty, complete domain is vacuously TRUE; clinical applicability needs a separate nonempty/eligibility guard.
An empty list of observed members is not a complete empty domain.
Two retrieved rows describing the same criterion identity count once.
Evidence for echo_action does not create a witness for a separate echo_speech category.
One observation can independently assert two different criteria; do not globally deduplicate by fact_id.
One positive in an incomplete domain leaves an unbounded possible count; missing members are not removed.
Two distinct positive witnesses establish at-least-two despite unobserved additional members.
Exactly-two is not established by two witnesses in an incomplete domain.
A tissue observation does not satisfy a blood predicate even for the same marker and patient.
A relative's phenotype is not the patient's phenotype.
The same metric with a supported explicit unit conversion satisfies a synthetic threshold.
PASP and mean_PAP are not interchangeable merely because both use mmHg.
Matching metric text with an incompatible unit is not a valid comparison.
TAPSE/PASP is not PASP; a ratio label cannot be shortened before binding.
Synthetic event_B occurs strictly after event_A within seven days.
Reversing event times does not preserve the before relation.
A missing event date remains UNKNOWN.
Positive and negative feature weights both contribute with their declared signs.
An unknown negative-weight feature yields a score interval, not zero contribution.
FALSE of a sufficient condition does not exclude the target.
A definite FALSE necessary conjunct can exclude when scope, source and authority are established.
Missing a necessary observation does not establish that the condition is FALSE.
A FALSE necessary condition cannot exclude when target applicability has not been established.
A plausible necessary condition is not automatically authorized for hard exclusion.
Two TRUE visible members cannot certify an incompletely extracted group; raw preview is kept separate.
One satisfied atom does not satisfy an AND-containing exclusion group.
A complete TRUE disjunct legitimately satisfies the exclusion root even if the other disjunct fails.
Not allowed to exclude sets an inference permission; it does not assert disease truth.
An exclusion permission denial blocks an otherwise triggered exclusion.
A TRUE disjunct does not hide a contradictory observation in the evaluated rule; hard effect waits for resolution.
A score result is emitted as a score, not a confirmation or exclusion.
A separately certified D implies A rule can be derived from D implies A AND B while inheriting parent scope and authority.
The truth-functional formula NOT(A implies NOT D) happens to be TRUE for A=TRUE,D=TRUE; this says nothing about permission to exclude. Policy V43 is a different output type.
Explicit opposite observations of a required proposition cannot be silently resolved by weighting or last-write-wins.
A runtime without certified decisive-negative evidence is not allowed to use a necessary FALSE for hard exclusion.
No atomic member may acquire a different relation/effect within this Rule.
Quantified arguments require an explicit bound variable and domain.
Repeated retrieval of the same score feature cannot create a second score term.
The same permission policy still prohibits the specified inference when an independent D-negative assertion is supplied; policy does not decide D truth.
For A=TRUE,D=FALSE, NOT(A implies NOT D) is FALSE, while the permission policy in V54 still applies. This distinguishes the output layers.
For unobserved A, A OR NOT A is UNKNOWN under K3; classical tautology elimination would change runtime behavior.
For the same empty observation model, literal TRUE is TRUE. V56/V57 are the cross-profile equivalence counterexample.
With A explicitly positive, A OR NOT A is TRUE; the unknown counterexample does not deny its classical tautology status.
With A explicitly negative, A OR NOT A is also TRUE; the classical comparison quantifies complete two-valued assignments.
